title: 〜がちだ
simpleExplanation: 〜がち means "tends to, is prone to" and describes something that happens more often than it should: skipping breakfast, getting sick, falling behind. The tendency is almost always undesirable.
whenUsed: Both registers. It attaches to a verb stem (抜きがち, 忘れがち, なりがち) or a noun (病気がち, 留守がち, 曇りがち). Before a noun it becomes がちな or がちの. Do not use it for good habits; for a slight current state use 〜気味.
formation: Vます + がち / N + がち

diagram.title: がち vs 気味 vs っぽい

rows.label: 〜気味
cells: 疲れ気味 (a bit tired now)

examples.ja: 最近、仕事が忙しくて、朝食を抜きがちだ。
examples.reading: さいきん、しごとがいそがしくて、ちょうしょくをぬきがちだ。
examples.en: Lately I'm busy with work and tend to skip breakfast.
examples.note: Vます + がち: a habit that has crept in.

examples.ja: 子供の頃は病気がちだった。
examples.reading: こどものころはびょうきがちだった。
examples.en: I was sickly as a child.
examples.note: N + がち: 病気がち = often ill.

examples.ja: 冬は運動不足になりがちです。
examples.reading: ふゆはうんどうぶそくになりがちです。
examples.en: In winter, one tends to get too little exercise.
examples.note: なりがち + です: polite general statement.

examples.ja: 一人暮らしだと、食事が偏りがちになる。
examples.reading: ひとりぐらしだと、しょくじがかたよりがちになる。
examples.en: When you live alone, your diet tends to become unbalanced.
examples.note: がちになる = start tending to.

examples.ja: 彼は最近、会議を休みがちだ。
examples.reading: かれはさいきん、かいぎをやすみがちだ。
examples.en: Lately he has been missing meetings a lot.

similarGrammar.difference: A slight, present state (風邪気味), not a repeated tendency.
An inherent quality (子供っぽい・忘れっぽい); がち is about frequency of events.
"Easy to / apt to", neutral; がち is negative and about habits.

commonMistakes.why: がち is reserved for undesirable tendencies.

commonMistakes.wrong: 今日は少し疲れがちだ。
commonMistakes.right: 今日は少し疲れ気味だ。
commonMistakes.why: A one-day state takes 気味; がち needs repetition over time.

commonMistakes.right: 病気がちな人 / 病気がちの人
commonMistakes.why: Before a noun, add な or の.

usageNotes: Frequent nouns: 病気がち, 留守がち, 曇りがち, 遠慮がち.
Frequent verbs: 忘れがち, 遅れがち, なりがち, 思いがち, 見落としがち.
遠慮がちに (hesitantly) is a common adverbial use.
jlptTips: A recurring bad habit (最近・つい・よく) with a Vます stem → がち; a slight state right now → 気味.
Distractors are 気味, っぽい, やすい. If the sentence describes a person's inherent character, っぽい; if a mild present symptom, 気味.
The noun-modifying form がちな is tested; options without な before a noun are traps.
